A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same CBraMod paper, with complete main text, references, and Appendices A–S. Text extraction and visual comparison support reliable comparison of the equations, tables, and figures.

before.justification: v5 reports original CBraMod benchmark evaluations, ablations, scaling experiments, and representation analyses in Section 3 and the appendices.

after.justification: v6 retains the original CBraMod evaluations and supplementary empirical analyses reported in v5.

M1.justification: Section 2 retains the same patching, masking, time-frequency encoder, asymmetric conditional positional encoding, criss-cross transformer, and reconstruction objective.

E1.justification: Both versions use TUEG pre-training and the same downstream coverage: the 12 datasets in Table 1 plus BCIC-IV-2a in Appendix E.9. The low-resource and leave-one-subject-out scenarios also already appear in v5.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged throughout, including Table 15’s nine baselines, the specialized sleep-staging baselines, and Appendix Q’s EEG-SimpleConv comparison.

E3.justification: Table 15 changes the reported BCIC-IV-2a metric headings from AUC-PR and AUROC to Cohen’s Kappa and Weighted F1. This aligns the table with the multiclass protocol already stated in Section 3.2 and Appendix D.3; it does not establish rerunning or changing the underlying evaluation. Other settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The attention, positional-encoding, and pre-training ablations are unchanged, as are the appendix analyses of scaling, segment length, fine-tuning, limited data, masking, interpretability, and convergence.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the five-random-seed reporting statement, means and standard deviations, and the same uncertainty reporting for the appendix experiments.

E6.justification: All numerical entries, rankings, and qualitative findings are retained. Table 15 keeps CBraMod’s values of 0.5138, 0.3518, and 0.4984, with identical standard deviations; its change corrects metric headings without adding or revising the numerical results.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and Equations (1)–(12) are unchanged. No formal assumption, derivation, theorem, or proof is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same architectural contributions, generalizability claims, and claims of state-of-the-art downstream performance.

C2.justification: The explanations of architectural benefits and generalization, the fine-tuning dependence discussed in Appendix J, and the limitations in Appendix S.2 are unchanged.

D1.justification: Software versions, preprocessing instructions, hyperparameters in Tables 5–6, hardware, training time, and the source-code access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The bibliography, Appendix A’s related-work discussion, and positioning relative to earlier EEG foundation models are unchanged.

P1.justification: The first-page arXiv stamp changes from v5 dated 13 April 2025 to v6 dated 6 November 2025. The narrative prose and section organization otherwise remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Table 15 replaces two column headings with Cohen’s Kappa and Weighted F1. Its structure and placement are retained, and no figures or tables are added, removed, or reorganized.

improvement.justification: Correcting Table 15’s metric headings resolves its inconsistency with the stated multiclass evaluation protocol and improves interpretation of the BCIC-IV-2a results. The gain is limited: the scientific content is otherwise unchanged, and Table 23 retains a similar inconsistency between its headings and accompanying discussion.
